sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house in Plymouth, MN?
sections.html:
You can list the house with an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is. Plymouth is a large west-metro suburb, so the right route depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close.

The city sits about 10 miles west of downtown Minneapolis and, at 81,026 people in the 2020 census, ranks as the seventh-largest city in Minnesota. A listing in Plymouth reaches a deep pool of buyers who commute along I-494, U.S. Highway 169 and Minnesota Highway 55. Homes in good shape and priced to the neighborhood tend to suit that route. Houses with deferred repairs, tenants in place, or an inherited estate to settle often fit a direct sale better.

  • Agent listing: widest exposure, but showings, repairs and a commission come with it.
  • For sale by owner: you keep the commission and handle pricing, paperwork and negotiation yourself.
  • Cash offer: a faster close on the house as it stands, usually at a price below a fully prepared listing.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau say about Plymouth's housing market?
sections.html:
Plymouth is an owner-heavy, high-value market. The table below pulls the figures that matter most to a seller from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for the city.

The city's population estimate is 2.6% below its April 2020 base, so the local buyer pool is steady rather than surging. Nearly 89% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which tells you most owners stay put for a long time before selling.

sections.h2: Which school district will a Plymouth buyer ask about?
sections.html:
Most Plymouth buyers want to know the district first, and the answer depends on which part of the city the house is in. Five districts serve Plymouth, so confirm the address before you advertise a school name.

  • Wayzata Public Schools (ISD 284): covers most of the city, especially the western, northwestern and southern areas.
  • Robbinsdale Area Schools (ISD 281): serves the east-central area.
  • Osseo (ISD 279): includes the northeast part of Plymouth.
  • Hopkins (ISD 270): reaches the southeast corner.

Wayzata High School sits in Plymouth and enrolls roughly 3,500 students in grades 9 to 12, which makes it the largest high school in Minnesota by enrollment. Families can also use open enrollment to attend a district other than the one that serves their address. Put the district on your listing sheet or in your cash-offer conversation, because it moves buyer interest more than most upgrades do.

sections.h2: How did Plymouth grow, and does its layout affect a sale?
sections.html:
Plymouth began as a farming town on the shores of Parkers Lake in the 1850s. It incorporated as a village on May 18, 1955, moved to council-manager government in 1968 and became a home rule charter city in 1992 when voters adopted a city charter.

Farming stayed the main occupation into the mid-1900s, and the suburban housing came after. Today the city counts about 300 miles of streets and 863 cul-de-sacs, so many homes sit on quiet curving blocks rather than a grid. Medicine Lake and Parkers Lake both lie within the city, and the Dakota people had an encampment on Medicine Lake long before settlers arrived. Houses near either lake draw their own group of buyers. The city's own welcome page for businesses describes Plymouth as home to more than 80,000 residents and nearly 53,000 jobs, which gives sellers a steady stream of relocating workers to market to.

The climate is humid continental, with winter lows averaging around 3 degrees Fahrenheit. Buyers' inspectors will look hard at the roof, gutters, attic insulation and furnace of any Plymouth house, so those items are worth checking before your first showing.

sections.h2: What should I know if my Plymouth house is a rental?
sections.html:
Plymouth requires a rental dwelling license for every rental, from a single-family home to a large complex. The license is valid for three years for one- and two-family homes and condominium units, and it runs annually for other dwelling types.

The city inspects apartment buildings every year and all other rental housing every three years. An owner or manager who handles more than one rental in Plymouth must finish a Crime Free Multi-Housing training before the license renews. Rental licenses cannot be transferred and are not refundable, which matters in a sale: a buyer who plans to keep the tenant must apply for a fresh license in the buyer's own name. Ask the city's Community and Economic Development department at 763-509-5430 for the current fee schedule before you set your price.

Plymouth also runs a lodging tax ordinance that covers short-term rentals. If you have rented the house by the night, ask the city how that tax applies before you close.

sections.h2: What disclosures and paperwork does a Plymouth sale require?
sections.html:
Minnesota law makes you give the buyer a written disclosure of material facts before you sign a purchase agreement. Under Minnesota Statutes section 513.55, that disclosure has to be made in good faith and reflect what you know about problems that could adversely and significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use of the property.

Wells are covered separately in section 103I.235: you tell the buyer in writing about any known well or state that you know of none. Many sellers can use the short "no known wells" line on the deed, but check the property for an old unsealed well first. When the sale closes, Hennepin County's recording office needs the deed, an electronic certificate of real estate value for any price over $3,000, a "send tax statements to" address and the well statement or certificate.

  • Recording is $46 per document, plus a $5 conservation fee where state deed tax is paid.
  • Deeds on properties with delinquent taxes cannot be transferred, so clear any balance first.
  • The county accepts documents by appointment at the Government Center, by eRecording through a title company, online through its Virtual Recorder site for a $3 service fee, or by mail.

The county's own page on recording land title documents lists the current fees and the deed tax calculator.

sections.h2: How are Plymouth property taxes handled at closing?
sections.html:
Hennepin County bills Plymouth property tax in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, and moves a due date to the next business day when it lands on a weekend or holiday. Because October 15 has already passed this year, the second half of 2026 should be paid or on its way by the time you list.

Late payments pick up a penalty under Minnesota Statutes section 279.01, and penalties continue to build monthly on any unpaid balance. If your lender escrows your taxes, ask the servicer for the payoff and escrow refund figures well before closing. Your title company will prorate the current year between you and the buyer. For a payment history or the status of a parcel, use the county's tax payment page or call its property tax line at 612-348-3011.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Plymouth house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, a house can be sold in its current condition. You still owe the buyer a written disclosure of material facts you know about. A traditional buyer will usually negotiate on inspection findings, while a cash buyer prices the repairs in and closes without asking you to fix them.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to sell a rental house in Plymouth?
faqs.a: You do not need a license to sell, but the rental dwelling license stays with you, not the house. It cannot be transferred, so the new owner applies on their own. Tell the buyer when your current license expires and when the next city inspection falls due.

faqs.q: Which Plymouth office records my deed?
faqs.a: Hennepin County's Recorder and Registrar of Titles records it, and city hall does not. You can book an in-person appointment at the Government Center in Minneapolis, send the deed by mail, use eRecording through your title company, or submit it online for a $3 service fee.

faqs.q: What happens if I owe back property tax on my Plymouth home?
faqs.a: The county will not transfer a deed on a property with delinquent taxes, so the balance and penalties have to be paid first, usually through the title company at closing. Call Hennepin County's property tax line at 612-348-3011 for an exact figure.

faqs.q: How do I find out which school district my Plymouth address belongs to?
faqs.a: Check the address with the district itself. Plymouth is split among Wayzata, Robbinsdale, Osseo and Hopkins, with Wayzata covering most of the city. A buyer who cares about a specific school will ask, so have the answer ready before your first showing.
